description: Establish an impartiality policy signed by top management. Map all personnel to potential conflicts of interest (financial, commercial, family ties with customers). Maintain a conflict-of-interest register reviewed at least annually. Ensure the organisational structure keeps testing decisions independent from commercial pressures.
evidenceSuggestion: Impartiality policy (Quality Manual); Conflict-of-interest register; Management commitment statement (signed); Organisation chart showing independence of technical functions
notes: Auditors verify that sales/business development and testing roles are organisationally separate. Each technical and management staff member must sign a declaration.

description: Have all laboratory personnel and contractors sign a confidentiality agreement before accessing customer samples or data. Document procedures for handling, storing, and releasing customer information. Obtain explicit customer consent before sharing results with any third party.
evidenceSuggestion: Signed confidentiality agreements (filed in personnel records); Confidentiality procedure in QMS; Customer contracts containing confidentiality clause
notes: Electronic data must have role-based access controls. Any legally required disclosure (e.g., to regulators) must be documented and, if possible, notified to the customer in advance.

description: Obtain and retain documentary evidence of the laboratory's legal entity status. If the laboratory is a department of a larger organisation, obtain a formal letter of delegation stating that the laboratory is legally responsible for its own testing activities.
evidenceSuggestion: Business registration certificate; OR Letter of delegation / authorisation from parent entity designating laboratory as legally responsible unit
notes: Keep a current copy in the QMS master file. Update if the corporate structure changes.

description: Prepare and maintain an up-to-date organisation chart with clear reporting lines. Issue written job descriptions specifying responsibilities and authorities for each role (Lab Manager, Technical Manager, Quality Manager, testing personnel). Designate and document a deputy for each key role to cover absences.
evidenceSuggestion: Organisation chart (version-controlled, dated); Job descriptions for each role; Deputy designation records
notes: Update the organisation chart within one week of any personnel change. Auditors will check that technical and quality functions are clearly assigned.

description: Define and document the laboratory's scope of activities specifying each test type, standard/method reference, test object/matrix, and measurand. Keep the internal scope document consistent with the AOSC-issued scope certificate. Notify AOSC before adding, removing, or changing any accredited method.
evidenceSuggestion: Scope of accreditation document (internal); AOSC accreditation certificate (current); Scope change notification records to AOSC
notes: Any method edition update (e.g., ISO 527:2012 → 2019) is a scope change requiring AOSC notification.

description: Establish documented processes ensuring all laboratory activities comply with the requirements of ISO/IEC 17025:2017, AOSC SR-01, and applicable national regulations. Identify and maintain awareness of all regulatory requirements relevant to accredited activities.
evidenceSuggestion: Quality Manual (cross-referenced to ISO 17025 clauses); Regulatory compliance register; Procedure for identifying applicable legal requirements
notes: Include in management review: any changes to regulations affecting the lab.

description: Ensure that personnel managing, performing, or verifying laboratory work have the authority and resources needed to fulfil their responsibilities. Document authority levels for approving test methods, releasing reports, and authorising deviation from procedures.
evidenceSuggestion: Authority matrix (who can approve what); Job descriptions with authority levels; Procedure for authorising deviations
notes: Authority to release accredited test reports must be explicitly documented and restricted to qualified, authorised personnel only.

description: Identify and document all resources required to perform each accredited test (personnel, facilities, equipment, reference materials, consumables, support services). Ensure resources are in place before accepting customer work. Review resource adequacy at management review.
evidenceSuggestion: Resource requirements list per test type; Management review minutes (resource adequacy agenda item)

description: Define and document minimum competence requirements for each function that influences laboratory results (testing personnel, technical reviewers, report approvers). Competence requirements shall specify: minimum education level, required experience (years and type), technical knowledge, and skills needed.
evidenceSuggestion: Competence requirements matrix (role × criterion); Job descriptions with minimum qualification requirements
notes: Competence criteria must be specific to the method group, not generic. E.g., 'can perform GC analysis of olefins per ASTM D6730' rather than 'laboratory skills'.

description: Verify that each person performing accredited testing meets the documented competence requirements before they are authorised to work independently. Use witnessed testing, practical examination, or review of training records and PT results as objective evidence of competence.
evidenceSuggestion: Witnessed test record / competence assessment form (signed by assessor and Technical Manager); Training completion records
notes: New personnel must be assessed before working unsupervised. Document the assessor's name, date, method tested, and outcome.

description: Implement a training programme covering: induction (QMS, safety, methods), method-specific technical training, and ongoing development. Evaluate and document the effectiveness of each training event. Update training needs assessment annually or when methods or equipment change.
evidenceSuggestion: Training plan / calendar (per person); Training records (course title, date, provider, duration, attendee signature); Training effectiveness evaluation records
notes: Training effectiveness can be demonstrated via practical assessment, written test, or satisfactory PT result after training.

description: Formally authorise each person to perform specific laboratory activities by issuing a signed authorisation record. Authorisation must be based on demonstrated competence. Maintain an up-to-date authorisation matrix showing which personnel are authorised for which methods.
evidenceSuggestion: Authorisation matrix (person × method, with authorisation dates); Individual authorisation letters or records signed by Technical Manager
notes: Authorisation must be renewed at least every three years or upon significant changes to a method or equipment (per SR-01 §6.2.2). Withdraw authorisation immediately if competence is in doubt.

description: Maintain an individual personnel file for each staff member performing laboratory activities. Files must include: qualifications (copies of degrees, certificates), training records, competence assessments, authorisation records, and any relevant experience documentation.
evidenceSuggestion: Personnel files containing: degree certificates; training records; competence assessment records; authorisation records; CV / experience summary
notes: Personnel files must be kept current. Retain records for the duration of employment plus the records retention period (minimum 5 years after last activity).

description: Ensure that personnel under training (probationers, students on placement) are supervised by authorised and competent personnel at all times when performing accredited tests. Document supervision arrangements. Do not release results produced by trainees without technical review by an authorised person.
evidenceSuggestion: Supervision plan / buddy assignment records; Test records signed by both trainee and supervisor
notes: Trainees must not sign off test results independently until full authorisation is granted.

description: Document the environmental requirements (temperature range, humidity, cleanliness level, vibration, lighting) for each testing area and for each test method that specifies environmental conditions. Ensure the actual facility conditions meet those requirements before testing begins.
evidenceSuggestion: Facility environmental requirements specification (per test area / method); Facility suitability assessment record
notes: Include environmental requirements in each method SOP. If a test method states 'temperature 23 ± 2 °C', that limit must appear in the environmental monitoring acceptance criteria.

description: Implement continuous or periodic monitoring of environmental conditions in all testing areas. Record all measurements. Define acceptance limits and actions to take when limits are exceeded (halt testing, document reason, re-test if results may have been affected).
evidenceSuggestion: Environmental monitoring logs (temperature, humidity — dated, signed); Calibration records for monitoring equipment; Out-of-limits action records
notes: QC-Olefins & UT: temperature + humidity log in chemistry lab. QC-Polyolefins: temperature log in mechanical test room. Frequency per method SOP (typically daily minimum, or continuous where critical).

description: Identify activities that could contaminate or interfere with each other (e.g., volatile solvents near moisture-sensitive samples, vibration from mechanical testing near precision balances). Implement physical separation, time scheduling, or containment to prevent cross-effects. Document arrangements.
evidenceSuggestion: Facility layout / floor plan showing separation arrangements; Procedure for incompatible activity scheduling

description: Control access to laboratory areas to prevent unauthorised entry that could affect test results or sample integrity. Document who is authorised to enter each area. Implement access control (key card, sign-in register, locked areas) appropriate to the sensitivity of activities performed.
evidenceSuggestion: Access control procedure; Visitor log; Access authorisation list per area
notes: Visitors accompanying samples to the test area must be documented. Customer sample storage areas must be locked or secured.

description: Implement good housekeeping measures in all testing areas to prevent cross-contamination between samples and between chemicals/reagents. Define cleaning procedures and cleaning schedules. Record cleaning activities where contamination could affect results.
evidenceSuggestion: Housekeeping / cleaning schedule and records; Procedure for preventing cross-contamination; Chemical storage segregation plan
notes: QC-Olefins & UT: solvent and reagent segregation critical. Separate storage for incompatible chemicals (acids/bases, oxidisers/reducers).

description: Prepare and maintain a master equipment register listing all measuring and testing equipment that influences results. Each entry must include: unique ID, equipment type, manufacturer, model, serial number, location, and current calibration/verification status. Ensure all required equipment is available and fit for use before accepting test work.
evidenceSuggestion: Equipment register (master list, version-controlled); Equipment inventory per testing area
notes: Include all instruments, balances, ovens, baths, mechanical testers, reference thermometers, and auxiliary devices that affect the result. Review and update the register at least annually.

description: When using equipment not under the laboratory's direct and permanent control (e.g., customer-provided equipment, leased instruments, equipment shared with another department), verify before each use that it meets the laboratory's specifications and calibration requirements. Document the verification.
evidenceSuggestion: Equipment verification record for each external-control equipment use; Agreement with equipment owner specifying responsibilities
notes: If the laboratory cannot ensure compliance for external equipment, it should not use it for accredited testing.

description: Before placing any new or returned-from-repair equipment into service, perform acceptance testing (commissioning check) to confirm the equipment meets specifications. Document the check: date, person, criteria used, results, and pass/fail outcome.
evidenceSuggestion: Equipment commissioning / acceptance test record (new equipment); Return-to-service check record (repaired / overhauled equipment)
notes: For a new analytical balance: verify linearity, repeatability, and eccentricity before first use. For a new tensile tester: verify load cell accuracy and crosshead speed accuracy.

description: Establish and maintain a calibration programme for all measuring equipment that influences results. Programme must specify calibration interval, calibration provider (accredited lab), and traceability chain. Apply calibration corrections (correction factors) to measurement results where required by the calibration certificate.
evidenceSuggestion: Calibration schedule / programme (per equipment ID); Current calibration certificates from accredited calibration labs; Correction factor records applied to results where applicable
notes: SR-01 Annex I sets maximum calibration intervals — do not exceed. Calibration must be performed by a VILAS-accredited or equivalent lab.

description: Designate reference standards (primary or secondary) used only for calibrating working instruments, not for routine testing. Physically segregate and label reference standards to prevent inadvertent use in testing. Document which instruments each reference standard calibrates.
evidenceSuggestion: Reference standard register; Reference standard usage log; Label on reference standards: 'REFERENCE STANDARD — calibration use only'
notes: Examples: reference weight set used only for balance calibration; reference thermometer used only for temperature instrument verification.

description: Establish a calibration programme specifically for reference standards, independent of working instrument calibrations. Calibration intervals for reference standards must be at least as frequent as those for the working instruments they calibrate.
evidenceSuggestion: Reference standard calibration certificates; Calibration programme showing reference standard calibration schedule
notes: Reference standards must be sent to a national metrology institute (VNMK) or ILAC MRA-accredited calibration lab for calibration.

description: Implement intermediate (in-service) checks for reference standards and critical working instruments between formal calibrations. Define the type, frequency, method, and acceptance criteria for each check. Record all check results. Investigate and act when a check fails.
evidenceSuggestion: Intermediate check procedure per instrument type; Intermediate check records (date, result, acceptance criteria, pass/fail, person performing check)
notes: Examples: analytical balance — daily single-point check with a class E2 or F1 reference weight; reference thermometer — quarterly comparison with VNMK certificate value at ice point.

description: Define and document the procedure for re-verifying equipment that has left the laboratory's direct control (sent for external calibration, repair, loan, or off-site use). Before returning equipment to service, confirm calibration status is valid and equipment functions correctly. Record the re-verification.
evidenceSuggestion: Return-to-service verification record (date, person, checks performed, calibration certificate reviewed, outcome)
notes: Even if the equipment came back with a new calibration certificate, perform a functional check before first use in accredited testing.

description: When laboratory software, LIMS, or automated equipment (e.g., automated titrators, integrated GC data systems) is used in accredited activities, validate or verify it before first use. Check that calculations, integrations, and data transfers produce correct results. Record validation.
evidenceSuggestion: Software validation / verification record; LIMS / instrument software version log; Validation test results (comparison of manual vs. automated calculation)
notes: After any software update, re-verify the affected functions before resuming accredited testing. Version control for calculation macros and worksheets is required.

description: Implement safeguards to prevent equipment from being accidentally or intentionally adjusted, modified, or tampered with in ways that would invalidate calibration. Use physical seals, tamper-evident labels, or software locks on adjustment functions. Record any authorised adjustments.
evidenceSuggestion: Tamper-evident seal records (calibration seals on balances, pressure gauges); Equipment adjustment authorisation log
notes: Calibration seals placed by the calibration lab must not be broken by lab personnel. If a seal is broken, the instrument must be re-calibrated before further use.

description: Attach a label or tag to every item of measuring equipment showing its unique ID, current calibration status (IN SERVICE / OUT OF SERVICE / LIMITED USE), and calibration expiry date. Use a consistent colour scheme. Remove or cover labels on equipment not fit for use.
evidenceSuggestion: Equipment status labels (physically present on instruments); Labelling procedure; Photographs or inspection records showing labels in place
notes: Recommended: green label = calibrated/in service; red label = out of service or expired. Calibration due date must be visible without moving the instrument.

description: Establish a clear procedure for taking equipment out of service when: calibration has expired, the instrument has produced suspect results, damage or malfunction is detected, or an intermediate check fails. Immediately label, segregate, and document affected equipment. Investigate the impact on previously reported results.
evidenceSuggestion: Out-of-service procedure; Out-of-service tag / record (date, reason, person); Impact assessment record for previous results potentially affected; Corrective action or customer notification records
notes: If suspect results were already reported to customers, initiate nonconforming work procedure (§7.10) and determine whether customer notification is required.

description: Maintain an individual equipment record (logbook or electronic record) for each item of measuring equipment. Records must include: equipment identity, receipt date, commissioning date, all calibration results and certificates, maintenance history, any damage, repair, or modification, and current status.
evidenceSuggestion: Individual equipment record / history card (per equipment ID) containing: calibration certificates; maintenance log; fault and repair records; commissioning record
notes: Equipment records are key audit evidence. Auditors trace the calibration chain for each instrument used in reported tests. Retain records for the life of the equipment plus 5 years.

description: Ensure that all measurement results used in accredited test reports are traceable to SI units through an unbroken chain of calibrations, each with documented measurement uncertainty. The chain must reach a national or international measurement institute (e.g., VNMK, NIST, PTB).
evidenceSuggestion: Calibration certificates showing traceability statements and measurement uncertainty; Traceability diagram / chain map for critical measurement parameters
notes: 'Traceable to SI' means the certificate must explicitly state traceability and include the calibration uncertainty.

description: Ensure that all reference materials and reference standards used in accredited activities are traceable to SI units or to certified reference values. Obtain and retain certificates of analysis (CoA) or calibration certificates for each reference material lot used.
evidenceSuggestion: Certificates of analysis / calibration certificates for all reference materials and standards (filed per lot number); Reference material register
notes: Reference materials must have: CRM number, property values with uncertainty, matrix, expiry date, and traceability statement.

description: Where SI traceability is technically not possible (e.g., certain chemical properties with no SI-traceable reference), document the alternative approach used, the rationale, and how confidence in measurement results is maintained. Report any such limitation to AOSC.
evidenceSuggestion: Documented justification for any non-SI-traceable measurement; AOSC notification record where applicable
notes: Rare for standard chemical/mechanical testing. Consult AOSC if a required reference standard does not exist.

description: Maintain an Approved Supplier List (ASL) for all external providers whose products or services affect test quality (calibration services, reference materials, subcontracted testing, critical consumables). Evaluate new suppliers before first use. Re-evaluate existing suppliers at defined intervals (annually recommended).
evidenceSuggestion: Approved Supplier List (name, service/product, evaluation date, criteria met, next review date); Supplier evaluation records (questionnaire responses, audit reports, or performance history)
notes: For calibration suppliers, check they are VILAS-accredited or equivalent ILAC MRA member. For CRM suppliers, verify ISO 17034 or ISO Guide 34 accreditation.

description: Communicate the laboratory's requirements clearly to each external provider before placing an order: specifications for products (grade, purity, lot-specific CoA), requirements for services (calibration scope, uncertainty target, traceability), and any acceptance criteria. Inspect and verify incoming items against requirements.
evidenceSuggestion: Purchase orders or specifications sent to suppliers; Incoming inspection / goods receipt records; Rejected goods records
notes: For critical reagents: confirm grade and lot CoA on receipt before using. For calibration certificates: confirm traceability statement and uncertainty before accepting the calibration.

description: Before accepting a test request, verify and document: (a) the method requested is within the accredited scope or can be performed competently; (b) required equipment and reference materials are available and in calibration; (c) the scope of work, sample type, and any customer requirements or specifications are understood. Record the review.
evidenceSuggestion: Contract review form / order acceptance checklist; Signed customer request form (method, sample type, quantities, required TAT); Method selection justification where non-standard method used
notes: Even for repeat/routine jobs, a documented confirmation that the lab can meet requirements is required. A purchase order number or customer email can serve as the request record.

description: Notify the customer promptly of any deviation from the agreed scope, method, or timeline discovered after work has started. Obtain customer agreement before changing the method or scope mid-work. Document all amendments to the original agreement and the customer's response. Retain all review records (original and amended).
evidenceSuggestion: Contract amendment records; Customer notification of deviations (email or written); Customer approval of method changes; Review record archive
notes: If the original method cannot be applied (e.g., sample volume insufficient), document the alternative agreed with the customer before proceeding.

description: Select test methods that are appropriate for the scope of testing, preferably published as national or international standards. For each standard method adopted, perform and document a formal verification demonstrating the lab can correctly apply it under its own conditions (at minimum: trueness via CRM/spike and repeatability, n ≥ 6). Ensure current editions of methods are in use and accessible.
evidenceSuggestion: Method library (current standard editions); Method verification protocol and report per method (trueness, repeatability data, acceptance criteria, conclusions); Method selection justification
notes: If a newer edition of the standard is published, re-verify the updated method before use. Notify AOSC of edition changes.

description: For non-standard, in-house developed, or modified methods, develop and execute a full validation plan before use. Validation must demonstrate fitness for purpose by establishing performance characteristics appropriate to the application (see SR-01 §7.2.2 for required parameters). Obtain customer agreement when using non-standard methods.
evidenceSuggestion: Validation plan (with scope, parameters, acceptance criteria); Validation data (raw data, statistical analysis); Validation report (signed by Technical Manager); Customer agreement record for non-standard methods
notes: Use SR-01 Table 1 as the parameter checklist for chemical methods. Document which parameters are not applicable and why.

description: If laboratory personnel perform or supervise sampling as part of the testing service, establish a sampling plan and sampling SOP. The plan must address: sampling location, method, sample size, labelling, preservation, and transport conditions. Record all sampling details in the test record.
evidenceSuggestion: Sampling SOP (if sampling is performed); Sampling records (location, date, person, method, conditions); Chain-of-custody record
notes: If the laboratory only receives samples already collected by customers, document this clearly. The lab is still responsible for checking sample condition on receipt (→ 7.4).

description: Implement a documented sample management procedure covering: receipt (condition check, unique ID assignment), storage (appropriate conditions per sample type), retention (duration), and disposal. Record any abnormal condition observed on receipt. Notify customers of damaged or unsuitable samples before testing.
evidenceSuggestion: Sample receipt log (date, ID, condition, storage location); Sample labelling system (unique ID on each container); Sample storage conditions procedure; Customer notification records for abnormal/unsuitable samples
notes: Samples must be traceable through every step from receipt to disposal. The unique sample ID must appear on all test records, worksheets, and the final test report.

description: Ensure that all test records contain sufficient information to reproduce the test: sample ID, date of test, method used, instrument used (with ID and calibration status), environmental conditions, raw observations, calculations, and identity of person performing and reviewing. Implement an amendment procedure: original entries preserved, amendments identified with date, reason, and initiator.
evidenceSuggestion: Completed test worksheets / bench records (raw data, not only final results); Amendment records (original value visible); Electronic data backup records
notes: Test records may be paper or electronic but must be legible, indelible (no correction fluid), and retrievable. Auditors will request raw data records for traceability to the final report.

description: Estimate and document measurement uncertainty (MU) for each quantitative test result within the accredited scope. Use either the bottom-up approach (ISO/IEC Guide 98 / TCVN 9595) or top-down approach (ISO 21748 / TCVN 10861). Prepare an MU budget per method identifying all significant uncertainty components. Report expanded uncertainty (U, k=2, 95 %) in test reports when relevant.
evidenceSuggestion: MU budget / uncertainty evaluation report per method; Supporting data (repeatability study, bias study, calibration uncertainty from certificates); MU reported in test report templates
notes: MU must be updated when method, equipment, or personnel change significantly. Minimum review every 5 years.

description: Implement a quality control (QC) monitoring programme to continuously verify the validity of results. This must include at minimum: use of certified reference materials (CRM) or control samples, duplicate analyses, and participation in PT schemes. Plot QC data on control charts. Define warning and action limits. Investigate and take corrective action when limits are exceeded.
evidenceSuggestion: QC monitoring plan per method (QC type, frequency, acceptance criteria); QC control charts (per method, per analyte); CRM use records; Duplicate analysis records; PT participation records and z-score reports
notes: QC monitoring data shall be reviewed at least monthly by the Technical Manager. Any trend toward out-of-control must trigger investigation before results are reported to customers.

description: Establish a report review and authorisation process: every test report must be reviewed for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with the method and customer requirements, then signed off by an authorised person before release. Maintain a log of all issued reports. Reports must be accurate, clear, unambiguous, and objective.
evidenceSuggestion: Report review checklist (completed per report); Authorisation record / signature on each report; Report issuance log
notes: The person authorising the report must be named on the authorisation matrix (§6.2.4). Electronic signatures are acceptable if the system prevents unauthorised approval.

description: Ensure every test report contains all mandatory common elements: unique report identification (number, date of issue), laboratory name and address, customer name and contact, unambiguous identification of each test item (description, condition, ID), date of receipt, date(s) of testing, results with units and measurement uncertainty, authorised signatory name and signature.
evidenceSuggestion: Test report template (reviewed against §7.8.2 checklist); Sample issued test reports; Report template review sign-off
notes: Run the §7.8.2 element checklist against current report templates before the next accreditation assessment. Update templates if any element is missing.

description: Include in every test report (in addition to §7.8.2 elements): the test method reference (standard number and edition), a statement of conformity or results with measurement uncertainty, any deviations from or additions to the test method, and the identity of the personnel performing the test.
evidenceSuggestion: Current test report templates (showing all §7.8.3 fields); Issued test reports demonstrating compliance with required elements
notes: The method reference must include the edition year (e.g., ISO 527-1:2019, not just ISO 527). If a deviation from the method occurred, it must be explicitly stated in the report.

description: If the laboratory issues calibration certificates (e.g., for customer-owned instruments calibrated in-house), include in each certificate: calibration results before and after adjustment (if any), the measurement uncertainty for each calibrated parameter, and a traceability statement. Note: applies only if calibration certificates are issued as part of laboratory activities.
evidenceSuggestion: Calibration certificate templates (if calibration services are offered); Calibration certificate review checklist
notes: If the laboratory does not issue calibration certificates, mark this clause as Not Applicable and document the justification.

description: When the test report includes results from sampling performed by laboratory personnel, include sampling details in the report: sampling date, sampling plan reference, sampling location, sampler name, and any environmental conditions at time of sampling that could affect the interpretation of results.
evidenceSuggestion: Test reports that include sampling information; Sampling record referenced in the report
notes: Only applicable when the laboratory performs sampling. If customer collects samples, note 'sampling by customer' in the report and disclaim responsibility for the sampling step.

description: When issuing statements of conformity (pass/fail against a specification), document the decision rule applied and state it in the report. Common decision rules: simple acceptance (result within tolerance = PASS), guard-band method (PASS only if result + uncertainty is within tolerance). Clearly label each result as 'PASS', 'FAIL', or 'Inconclusive' with the specification and decision rule referenced.
evidenceSuggestion: Decision rule policy (which rule is applied and when); Test report templates showing statement-of-conformity format; Customer agreements on decision rule where applicable
notes: ISO/IEC 17025:2017 Annex A explains decision rules. Agree the decision rule with the customer before reporting. The rule must be stated in the report, not just in internal procedures.

description: When test reports include opinions or interpretations (e.g., 'material is suitable for application X' or 'result indicates contamination'), document the basis for the opinion (expertise, comparison with published data, regulatory thresholds). Clearly identify opinions/interpretations as such in the report, distinguishing them from measured results.
evidenceSuggestion: Documented basis for opinions in test records; Procedure for issuing opinions and interpretations; Opinions clearly labelled in report template
notes: Only personnel with demonstrated expertise in the relevant field should issue opinions. The authorising person's qualifications must support the opinion given.

description: Establish a procedure for amending issued test reports. Amendments must be clearly identified as amendments (e.g., 'Amendment No. 1 to Report No. XXX'). The original report must be identified, and the changed information must be highlighted or listed. Document why the amendment was issued. Notify all parties who received the original report.
evidenceSuggestion: Report amendment procedure; Amended report (showing original report number, amendment number, and changed items); Notification records sent to customers holding original report
notes: Amendments must go through the same review and authorisation process as original reports. Retain both original and amendment.

description: Implement a complaints procedure: provide a complaints mechanism to customers (form, email, telephone), acknowledge receipt within a defined timeframe, investigate root causes objectively (involve independent person where possible), decide and implement resolution, notify the complainant of the outcome and expected timeline.
evidenceSuggestion: Complaints procedure; Complaints log (complaint reference, date, description, investigation outcome, resolution, closure date); Customer notification of complaint outcome
notes: All complaints must be logged, even those resolved informally. Trend analysis of complaints to be included at management review.

description: Implement a nonconforming work procedure: define trigger events that constitute nonconforming work (equipment out of calibration during testing, out-of-range QC check, incorrect method applied). Designate authority to stop work. Document the nonconformity, assess its impact on past results, notify affected customers if results are compromised, and initiate corrective action.
evidenceSuggestion: Nonconforming work procedure; Nonconformance report (NCR) log (each event: date, description, impact assessment, customer notification record, corrective action reference); Customer notification letters/emails where applicable
notes: Not every QC failure requires customer notification — the impact assessment determines this. Systematic failures (e.g., all balances uncalibrated for 6 months) require notification of all customers whose results may be affected.

description: Implement data integrity and information management controls: validate all calculation worksheets, macros, and LIMS before use; implement version control for all calculation tools; protect electronic data from unauthorised modification (role-based access, audit trail); establish and test a backup and data recovery procedure.
evidenceSuggestion: Data management procedure; LIMS / calculation tool validation records; Access control records; Backup schedule and recovery test records; Version history for calculation templates
notes: Auditors may request to trace a reported value back through the calculation to the raw instrument reading. Any unexplained gap in this chain is a major nonconformity.

description: Decide and document which management system option the laboratory implements: Option A (explicit requirements of Clauses 8.2–8.9) or Option B (ISO 9001-aligned system that fulfils the intent of Clauses 8.2–8.9). State the chosen option in the Quality Manual and ensure all elements required by the chosen option are in place.
evidenceSuggestion: Quality Manual (section declaring Option A or B); ISO 9001 certificate (if Option B)
notes: Most testing-only labs use Option A. If ISO 9001 is already certified (Option B), cross-reference QMS procedures to each ISO 17025:2017 clause to demonstrate coverage.

description: Establish and maintain a Quality Manual (or equivalent documented management system) covering: the laboratory's quality policy, quality objectives (measurable, time-bound), how each clause of ISO 17025:2017 is addressed, and reference to all supporting procedures. Communicate the Quality Policy to all personnel.
evidenceSuggestion: Quality Manual (current version, signed by Lab Director); Quality Policy (posted or distributed to all staff); Quality Objectives register (with targets and owners)
notes: Quality Objectives must be measurable. Example: 'PT z-score ≤ 2 for 100% of rounds in 2026' or 'All calibrations completed on schedule — zero overdue by Q4 2026'.

description: Implement a document control system: assign unique document IDs and revision numbers; require review and approval signatures before issue; maintain a master document list with current revisions; ensure only current versions are available at points of use; prevent unintended use of obsolete documents (mark 'OBSOLETE' and remove or archive).
evidenceSuggestion: Master document list / document register (ID, title, revision, effective date, location); Document approval signatures on each controlled document; Obsolete document archive with access restriction
notes: Electronic document management: restrict editing access to document controller. Paper documents: all copies must be controlled copies (stamped or numbered).

description: Establish a records retention schedule specifying: record type, minimum retention period (test records: minimum 5 years per SR-01), storage location, format, and authorised disposal method. Ensure records are legible, stored to prevent damage or loss, and retrievable within a reasonable time when requested by AOSC.
evidenceSuggestion: Records retention schedule; Record storage procedure (physical + electronic); Backup verification records; Records disposal log (for records reaching end of retention period)
notes: Key retention periods (minimum): test reports and raw data — 5 years; calibration certificates — life of equipment + 5 years; competence records — employment + 5 years. Customer contracts may specify longer periods.

description: Conduct a risk assessment covering all laboratory activities at least annually. Identify risks that could affect the validity of test results, laboratory impartiality, or customer confidence. Assign risk levels (likelihood × impact). Implement mitigation actions for significant risks. Track actions to closure.
evidenceSuggestion: Risk register (risk ID, description, likelihood, impact, rating, mitigation action, owner, due date, status); Risk assessment review records; Management review minutes (risk discussion item)
notes: Also identify opportunities for improvement. Risk register must be updated when significant changes occur (new methods, key personnel departure, new equipment, scope changes).

description: Identify improvement opportunities from multiple sources: internal audits, PT results, customer feedback, complaints, corrective actions, management review outputs, and personnel suggestions. Document, prioritise, assign, and track improvement actions. Evaluate whether implemented improvements achieved the intended effect.
evidenceSuggestion: Improvement register / action tracker (source, description, action, owner, target date, completion date, effectiveness review); Management review minutes showing improvements discussed
notes: At minimum, improvement opportunities from management review must be documented with specific actions, owners, and deadlines.

description: Implement a corrective action procedure: when nonconformities are identified (from any source), perform root cause analysis, implement corrective actions to eliminate root causes (not just the symptoms), review effectiveness after implementation, and close the action when verified as effective. Update risk register if the nonconformity reveals a new risk.
evidenceSuggestion: Corrective action log (CAR number, source, description, root cause analysis, actions taken, responsible person, target date, effectiveness review, closure date); Root cause analysis evidence (5-Why, fishbone, etc.)
notes: Auditors distinguish between correction (fixing the immediate problem) and corrective action (preventing recurrence). Both must be documented. Repeat nonconformities indicate ineffective corrective actions.

description: Prepare and execute an annual internal audit programme covering all ISO 17025:2017 clauses and all accredited test methods. Internal auditors must be trained and independent from the area being audited. Document audit findings, evidence reviewed, and any nonconformities. Follow up on findings to verify corrective actions are implemented and effective before closing.
evidenceSuggestion: Annual internal audit programme / schedule; Audit checklists (per clause and per method); Audit reports (with findings and evidence); Corrective action records for audit findings; Auditor training / qualification records
notes: Plan audit timing so findings can be addressed before the annual AOSC assessment. All clauses must be covered within the 12-month cycle. At least one method audit per accredited test discipline required.

description: Conduct a formal management review meeting at least once per year. Agenda must include all §8.9.2 input items: PT trends, audit findings, corrective actions, customer feedback, complaints, resource adequacy, risk update, and scope/policy changes. Document decisions, action items, owners, and deadlines. Distribute minutes to all relevant personnel.
evidenceSuggestion: Management review agenda (covering §8.9.2 inputs); Meeting minutes (decisions and action items); Attendance records; Action item tracking from previous review
notes: Top management (Lab Director or equivalent) must chair or formally attend. Review outputs (action items) must be tracked and status reported at the following review.

text: AOSC SR-01 SUPPLEMENTARY REQUIREMENTS — Rev 05 (30 Oct 2025)

description: Demonstrate that the laboratory has analysed and identified risks that could impact its impartiality, and has taken actions to eliminate those risks. Maintain documented evidence of the impartiality risk analysis, reviewed at least annually. Assessors will verify that commercial, financial, or personnel-related pressures cannot override technical decisions.
evidenceSuggestion: Impartiality risk analysis record (annually updated); Management commitment statement referencing impartiality; Conflict-of-interest register; Organisation chart showing separation of testing decisions from commercial functions
notes: SR-01 §4.1 supplements ISO 17025 §4.1. The standard text: 'Testing/Calibration laboratory shall have evidence showing that they have analyzed and identified to eliminate risks that impact on the laboratory's impartiality.' Key word: 'evidence' — documented proof, not just a policy statement.

description: Establish a confidentiality policy appropriate to the laboratory's operations and make it publicly available to all interested parties (staff, customers/clients, other relevant parties). The policy must address how customer data, test results, and samples are protected from unauthorised disclosure.
evidenceSuggestion: Written confidentiality policy (posted on notice board or website, or distributed to customers); Signed confidentiality agreements for staff and external parties; Customer contracts containing confidentiality clause; Evidence policy is communicated to interested parties
notes: SR-01 §4.2 supplements ISO 17025 §4.2. The standard text: 'The laboratory shall establish a confidentiality policy suitable with its operation and shall public this policy to the interested party (staffs, customer/clients, other relevant parties,...ect).' Note 'public' means make publicly available — not just internal.

description: Ensure that the laboratory's management system documentation explicitly references: (1) signatory authorities (who is authorised to sign accredited test reports), (2) the area where ISO/IEC 17025 applies, (3) the accredited scope, and (4) the laboratory location(s) — permanent facilities, onsite facilities, or mobile facilities. Keep these references current after every scope change or personnel change.
evidenceSuggestion: Quality Manual (section identifying signatory authorities, scope, and locations); Authorised signatory list (names, roles, specimen signatures); AOSC accreditation certificate showing accredited scope and location; Document control records for QM updates
notes: SR-01 §5.1 supplements ISO 17025 §5. The standard text: 'Management system document shall reference to signatory authorities, area apply ISO/IEC 17025, accredited scope, laboratories location (permanent facilities, onsite facilities or in mobile facilities,...)' Assessors check that the QM clearly names who can sign accredited reports.

description: Where the laboratory does not apply any requirement of ISO/IEC 17025 (e.g., sampling per §7.3, or calibration certificate issuance per §7.8.4 because the lab only performs testing), document a clear written statement with justification explaining why the requirement does not apply. This statement must be in the management system documentation and reviewed at each management review.
evidenceSuggestion: Quality Manual section listing non-applicable requirements with justifications (e.g., '§7.3 Sampling — not applicable: the laboratory does not perform sampling; all samples are customer-supplied'); Management review records confirming non-applicabilities remain valid
notes: SR-01 §5.2 supplements ISO 17025 §5. The standard text: 'The laboratory shall have a clear statement with justification when the laboratory does not apply any requirement of the standard.' This is specifically about documented justification for exclusions — not just saying 'N/A'.

description: Ensure that AOSC assessment teams are given unrestricted access to all relevant divisions, departments, and support areas of the organisation to verify conformity with ISO/IEC 17025 during assessment. This includes support functions such as procurement, HR, IT (for data management), and management. Do not restrict assessors to the bench area only.
evidenceSuggestion: Documented policy or procedure for hosting AOSC assessments (access commitment); Assessment hosting checklist (areas to be made available); Previous assessment records showing all relevant areas were accessible
notes: SR-01 §5.3 supplements ISO 17025 §5. The standard text: 'The assessment team shall be allowed to assess the activities of relevant divisions to verify its conformity with the standard.' Restricting assessors from support divisions (e.g., denying access to purchasing records or HR files) is a nonconformity.

description: Document and maintain a competence profile (including training records) and job description for all laboratory personnel. Ensure records of skills assessments for all personnel conducting accredited tests are available and updated at least every 12 months per group of test parameters. Skills assessment records must be available at assessment.
evidenceSuggestion: Individual competence profiles (per person: education, experience, training, skills assessment outcomes); Job descriptions for all roles; Skills assessment records dated within the past 12 months per parameter group; Authorisation matrix per method
notes: SR-01 §6.2 (General) supplements ISO 17025 §6.2. Key requirement: skills assessment per group of parameters, minimum every 12 months. 'Group of parameters' = related methods (e.g., all GC methods, all MFI methods). Assessors will request to see these records for all actively testing personnel.

description: Demonstrate that training needs are formally analysed at least annually (e.g., via gap analysis between current competence and required competence). Maintain records showing that training actually occurred during each year (training log with dates, topics, duration, and attendees). Evaluate effectiveness of training and retain effectiveness assessment records.
evidenceSuggestion: Training needs analysis record (annual, per person or per method group); Annual training plan / calendar; Training attendance records (date, topic, provider, duration, names); Training effectiveness evaluation records (test, practical assessment, or PT result post-training)
notes: SR-01 §6.2 (General) requires evidence of both: (1) training needs analysis occurred, and (2) training actually took place. A plan alone is insufficient — records of training execution must also exist. Assessors may ask to see records from the past 12 months.

description: Personnel authorised to independently sign off on accredited test results (authorization competence) must have: (1) professional qualifications relevant to the assigned testing field; (2) if the qualification is in a different field — documented evidence of relevant training AND at least 12 months of relevant experience; (3) at least 12 months of experience in the specific accredited testing field.
evidenceSuggestion: Degree certificates (relevant field confirmed); Experience records (employment history, duration in current testing role); Cross-field training records and experience calculation where applicable; Authorisation records per method signed by Technical Manager
notes: SR-01 §6.2.1 sets minimum competence criteria for authorised personnel (those who sign/approve accredited reports). '12 months in the accredited testing field' means hands-on testing experience, not general lab experience. If a chemist does polymer mechanical testing: need 12 months specific mechanical testing experience plus evidence of relevant training.

description: Personnel performing accredited tests as technicians (analyst/technician level) must have: (1) professional qualifications relevant to the testing/calibration field; (2) at least 3 months of experience conducting the specific accredited tests; (3) if from a different qualification field — documented evidence of relevant training AND at least 12 months experience. Probationary analysts must work under continuous monitoring by a competent analyst until their training is complete.
evidenceSuggestion: Personnel files: degree certificates, hire date, start-of-testing date; Probationary supervision plan and records (signed by supervisor and trainee); Competence declaration / authorisation sign-off after probation; Cross-field training records where applicable
notes: SR-01 §6.2.2 sets criteria for technician-level analysts (vs. §6.2.1 for authorisation). The 3-month threshold applies from the start of performing the specific accredited test. Probationals MUST be supervised — their results must be reviewed by an authorised analyst before release.

description: SR-01 §6.3.1 (Microbiology), §6.3.2 (Molecular Biology), and §6.3.3 (Pharmaceutical laboratory) sections are NOT APPLICABLE to this laboratory. Central Laboratory performs chemical testing (QC-Olefins & UT) and mechanical testing (QC-Polyolefins) only. No microbiological, molecular biology, or pharmaceutical accredited activities are conducted.
evidenceSuggestion: Quality Manual non-applicability statement (SR-01 §6.3.1, §6.3.2, §6.3.3 excluded with justification); AOSC accreditation certificate confirming scope is chemical and mechanical testing only
notes: SR-01 §6.3.1 = Microbiology requirements; §6.3.2 = Molecular Biology; §6.3.3 = Pharmaceutical lab. None applicable to this chemical/mechanical lab. Status set to 'Not Applicable' — no action required. Document this exclusion explicitly in the QMS per SR-01 §5.2.

description: Document criteria for equipment acceptance before placing new equipment into service (specifications, calibration requirements, functional checks). After any calibration, maintenance, or repair: verify that the equipment meets acceptance criteria before returning it to service for accredited testing. Record each return-to-service verification.
evidenceSuggestion: Equipment acceptance criteria (per equipment type or model); Return-to-service verification records (date, equipment ID, checks performed, outcome, authorising person); Equipment history files linking calibration certificates to return-to-service checks
notes: SR-01 §6.4.1 supplements ISO 17025 §6.4. The 'verify before return to service' requirement means a functional check AFTER receiving back from external calibration — even if a new certificate was issued. Typical check: balance → single-point weight verification; GC → single-point calibration curve run; Tensile tester → load cell check.

description: Calibration and intermediate check intervals for all measuring and testing equipment shall comply with the maximum intervals specified in SR-01 Annex I (or Annex II-V where applicable). For any equipment performing internal calibration: maintain a written procedure for the calibration, appropriate measurement standards, trained personnel, and suitable environmental conditions. Document all internal calibration activities.
evidenceSuggestion: Equipment calibration schedule (cross-referenced to SR-01 Annex I intervals); Current calibration certificates (all within validity period); Internal calibration procedure(s) where applicable; Records of internal calibration activities (date, method, standard used, result, person, environmental conditions)
notes: SR-01 Annex I specifies maximum calibration intervals for specific equipment types (e.g., GC temperature: 1 year; balance: 1 year; MFI temperature: 1 year; density floats: verify against current Annex I). Do not exceed the maximum interval. Internal calibration is only allowed if the lab has the required procedure, reference standards, trained staff, and environmental controls.

description: All reference materials, certified reference materials (CRMs), and test media used in accredited testing must have a clear origin and a Certificate of Analysis (CoA) or equivalent document issued by a competent supplier. Preferentially use ISO 17034-certified CRMs where available. For all chemicals/reagents that affect test results: check quality prior to use by lot number and maintain records of all quality checks performed.
evidenceSuggestion: Reference material and CRM register (origin, supplier, lot number, CoA on file, receipt date, expiry date, storage, status); CoA archive (filed by lot); Lot quality check records (date, lot, check performed, result, acceptance/rejection); ISO 17034 or equivalent accreditation for CRM suppliers (where available)
notes: SR-01 §6.4.2 supplements ISO 17025 §6.5.2. The 'check prior to use by lot' requirement means each new lot must be verified before use in accredited testing — e.g., open a CRM lot, run against an existing verified lot; or run a reagent lot against the previous lot's results to confirm performance. Record this check even if the result confirms the lot is acceptable.

description: Equipment having a significant effect on reported results must be calibrated by an appropriate calibration laboratory as specified in AOSC GR-14. Maintain CRM records including: sufficient reference materials, full identity and source records, complete documentation of property values and associated measurement uncertainty. Assign unique codes to all reference materials. Maintain documented procedures for acquisition, preservation, maintenance, and confirmation of RMs. Purchase records for RMs must include: property values and MU, certificate validity period, and required storage conditions.
evidenceSuggestion: Calibration certificates from AOSC GR-14 compliant providers; RM/CRM register with unique codes, property values, MU, validity, storage conditions; RM procedures (acquisition, preservation, maintenance, confirmation); Purchase records for each RM lot; AOSC GR-14 document on file
notes: SR-01 §6.5 supplements ISO 17025 §6.5. 'AOSC GR-14' is the AOSC general requirement document specifying which calibration laboratories are acceptable (VILAS-accredited or equivalent ILAC MRA member). RM purchase records must include MU of certified values — a CoA without stated uncertainty does not satisfy this requirement.

description: When the laboratory subcontracts testing activities, use only competent subcontractors. A competent subcontractor is: (1) an AOSC-accredited facility for the relevant tests, OR (2) a laboratory accredited by a mutual recognition partner of AOSC (ILAC MRA member), OR (3) a government-designated testing facility. The laboratory remains fully responsible for the subcontracted results issued to customers. Regularly review the subcontractor's accreditation status.
evidenceSuggestion: Subcontracting procedure; List of approved subcontractors with their accreditation body and certificate number; Copies of subcontractor accreditation certificates (current); Records of regular accreditation status checks (e.g., annual VILAS register check); Customer notification records where subcontracting was used
notes: SR-01 §6.6.1 supplements ISO 17025 §6.6. If the laboratory does not subcontract, document this fact. 'Regular review' of accreditation status means checking at least annually that the subcontractor's accreditation has not been suspended or withdrawn. Accreditation can be suspended without notice — check the VILAS public register.

description: Define and document clear criteria for the evaluation and selection of all external suppliers of chemicals, reference standards, strains, and services (calibration, proficiency testing, etc.). Apply these criteria when selecting new suppliers. Maintain records of the evaluation of products and services before use (incoming inspection, review of certificates, supplier performance assessment).
evidenceSuggestion: Supplier evaluation criteria (documented: e.g., accreditation status, technical capability, past performance, cost); Approved Supplier List with evaluation dates and outcomes; Incoming inspection records (chemicals: CoA checked, grade confirmed; calibration: certificate reviewed for traceability and MU; PT providers: ISO 17043 accreditation confirmed)
notes: SR-01 §6.6.2 supplements ISO 17025 §6.6.2. The requirement explicitly covers suppliers of calibration services and PT providers — not just chemical suppliers. For PT providers: verify ISO/IEC 17043 accreditation before each round. For calibration labs: verify current VILAS or ILAC MRA accreditation at each annual re-evaluation.

description: The laboratory shall have documented test methods that are referenced, verified, validated, and quoted in test reports. Maintain procedures for method selection and validation. Retain all verification and validation records; these records will be reviewed by AOSC during assessment. Always use updated editions of test methods — when a new version is published, the laboratory has a maximum of 12 months to update and implement the new method.
evidenceSuggestion: Method library (current edition of each standard method); Method selection procedure; Verification/validation records per method; Document control records showing edition updates and implementation dates; Test reports citing method standard and edition year
notes: SR-01 §7.2.1 supplements ISO 17025 §7.2. The 12-month update rule is strict — if ISO 527-1:2012 is superseded by ISO 527-1:2019, the lab must verify and implement the 2019 edition within 12 months of its publication date. Failure to update = using an outdated method = potential scope deviation. Notify AOSC when adopting the new edition.

description: During AOSC assessment, the laboratory must be prepared for test witnessing: for initial accreditation and re-assessment, at least 30% of accredited tests in the scope must be witnessed by assessors. For surveillance assessments, the number of tests to be witnessed is √N (square root of total number of accredited tests per field, rounded up). Ensure all required equipment, samples, and personnel are available during assessment visits.
evidenceSuggestion: Test witnessing schedule prepared for each AOSC assessment visit; List of accredited tests per field (to calculate √N for surveillance); Samples/specimens prepared and available; Personnel roster for assessment days confirming competent staff available to perform tests
notes: SR-01 §7.2.1 test witness requirement: Initial/re-assessment = ≥30% of accredited tests must be witnessed. Surveillance (SA1, SA2, etc.) = √N tests (e.g., if N=20 accredited tests in a field, √20 ≈ 5 tests must be witnessed). Pre-assess which tests to prepare; have reagents, samples, and standards ready before the assessor arrives.

description: Verify or validate all methods before use in accredited testing, assessing both basic conditions and all technical factors affecting results. For standard methods that include precision data (repeatability r and reproducibility R): perform a verification demonstrating the lab can achieve those published precision values. For non-standard or in-house methods: perform a full validation. Review all verification and validation records at least every 24 months.
evidenceSuggestion: Verification protocol and report per standard method (with comparison to published r/R values); Validation protocol and report per non-standard or in-house method; V&V record index with review dates (next review date ≤ 24 months from last review); Technical Manager sign-off on each V&V report
notes: SR-01 §7.2.2 supplements ISO 17025 §7.2.2. The 24-month periodic review is an AOSC-specific additional requirement. At each review: assess whether the V&V data still reflects current lab conditions (same equipment, same personnel, same reagents). If significant changes occurred, a new V&V study may be required rather than just a paper review.

description: Submit all method verification and validation records to AOSC before the initial accreditation assessment. If a method is updated during the accreditation cycle (new standard edition adopted), inform AOSC and submit the updated V&V records within 30 days of implementation. For chemical test methods, the validation must address all applicable parameters in SR-01 Table 1: Trueness, Sensitivity, Selectivity, Repeatability, Reproducibility, LOD, LOQ, Linearity, Working Range, and Measurement Uncertainty.
evidenceSuggestion: AOSC submission records for V&V reports (before initial assessment); Notifications sent to AOSC for method updates with V&V records attached (within 30 days); V&V reports for chemical methods showing all SR-01 Table 1 parameters addressed or justified as non-applicable
notes: SR-01 Table 1 (10 parameters for chemical methods): Trueness, Sensitivity, Selectivity, Repeatability, Reproducibility, LOD, LOQ, Linearity, Working Range, Uncertainty. Each must either be determined or documented as not applicable with justification. For mechanical methods (QC-Polyolefins): SR-01 does not specify Table 1 — focus on repeatability, reproducibility, and MU.

description: Evaluate measurement uncertainty (MU) for all quantitative accredited test results using either ISO 21748 (TCVN 10861) — the top-down approach — or ISO/IEC Guide 98-3 (TCVN 9595) — the bottom-up GUM approach. Both approaches are acceptable to AOSC. Calibration laboratory MU shall be evaluated per AOSC GR-12. Report expanded uncertainty (U, coverage factor k=2, ~95% confidence) in test reports where required.
evidenceSuggestion: MU evaluation reports per accredited method (approach: ISO 21748 or ISO/IEC Guide 98; components; combined uncertainty; U at k=2); Supporting data (repeatability study, bias study, calibration cert uncertainty values); MU stated in test report templates; AOSC GR-12 document (if calibration activities performed)
notes: SR-01 §7.6 supplements ISO 17025 §7.6. References: ISO 21748 = TCVN 10861 (top-down, uses reproducibility data); ISO/IEC Guide 98-3 = TCVN 9595 (GUM bottom-up). Most chemical labs use ISO 21748 as it leverages the validation/reproducibility data already collected. GR-12 applies specifically to calibration laboratories — verify if this lab issues calibration certificates.

description: Implement quality assurance (QA) activities to ensure the validity of internal test results. For each method, define the type of QA activity (e.g., CRM check, control sample, duplicate, blank, spike recovery), the frequency, and the acceptance criteria. Maintain all QA activity records systematically and review them regularly to detect trends before they result in out-of-control results.
evidenceSuggestion: QA/QC plan per method (QA activity type, frequency, acceptance criteria); QC run records / control charts; CRM check records; Duplicate analysis records; Out-of-control event investigation records; QA data review sign-off (monthly or per batch)
notes: SR-01 §7.7.1 supplements ISO 17025 §7.7. The standard text: '(a) Activity to ensure quality of internal test results, determine frequency, maintain records.' §7.7.1(b) covers microbiology positive/negative controls — NOT APPLICABLE to this lab. Key AOSC expectation: QA activities must be defined per method, not just generically. Assessors will check control charts for trends.

description: Participate in external comparison activities at least once per year for each accredited sub-field, through one of the following: (a) proficiency testing (PT) by a competent PT provider accredited under ISO/IEC 17043 or accepted by AOSC; (b) if no appropriate PT scheme exists — interlaboratory comparison (ILC) with other AOSC-accredited ISO 17025 laboratories; (c) if neither PT nor ILC is available — use at least 2 internal alternative methods (e.g., CRM checks, retained sample re-testing, repeatability/reproducibility assessment, intra-lab comparison).
evidenceSuggestion: Annual PT participation plan (per sub-field, per PT provider, per round date); PT result reports and z-scores (all rounds in past 12 months); PT provider ISO 17043 accreditation certificate; If ILC used: ILC protocol and results; If internal alternatives: documented evidence of ≥2 methods with records
notes: SR-01 §7.7.2 supplements ISO 17025 §7.7.2. Priority: (a) PT first, then (b) ILC, then (c) internal alternatives. For each sub-field (e.g., GC hydrocarbon analysis, MFI, density), at least one round per year. Unsatisfactory PT result (|z|>3) = nonconformity requiring root cause analysis and corrective action before next assessment.

description: Clearly identify the accreditation status of each test result in the test report — for example, mark non-accredited results with an asterisk (*) or equivalent notation. Use the AOSC accreditation symbol and accreditation number in accordance with AOSC GR-02. For test results not covered by the accredited scope, do not use the VILAT or VLAC accreditation symbol.
evidenceSuggestion: Test report templates showing: (1) marking for non-accredited results (e.g., '*'), (2) AOSC accreditation symbol and number (per GR-02), (3) scope statement; AOSC GR-02 document on file; Sample issued test reports demonstrating correct identification of accredited vs. non-accredited results
notes: SR-01 §7.8 supplements ISO 17025 §7.8. Three key requirements: (1) identify accredited vs. non-accredited results in each report; (2) use AOSC symbol per GR-02 format and placement rules; (3) never use VILAT or VLAC symbol for out-of-scope results. Mix of accredited and non-accredited results in same report is allowed if clearly distinguished. Obtain GR-02 from AOSC and review all report templates against its requirements.

description: Retain all quality and technical records for a minimum of 5 years, unless other applicable regulations prescribe a longer period. Records include: test records, test reports, calibration certificates, competence records, internal audit records, corrective action records, V&V records, and management review minutes. Apply longer retention periods where legally required or where customer contracts specify longer.
evidenceSuggestion: Records retention schedule (record type, minimum period, location, disposal method); Records storage procedure; Disposal log (for records that have reached end of retention period); Any applicable legal or contractual retention requirements identified
notes: SR-01 §8.4 supplements ISO 17025 §8.4 with an explicit 5-year minimum. The standard text: 'The laboratory shall retain records for ≥5 years unless otherwise prescribed.' Customer contracts in the petrochemical sector sometimes require longer retention (e.g., 10 years) — check each major customer contract. Equipment records: retain for life of equipment + 5 years (calibration history must be traceable for the instrument's full service life).

description: As an extension of the impartiality requirements in SR-01 §4.1, the laboratory shall demonstrate: (1) analysis of context (internal and external factors affecting the lab), (2) identification and assessment of risks and opportunities, and (3) implementation of appropriate actions to control identified risks. This goes beyond simply listing risks — the lab must show actions taken and their effectiveness.
evidenceSuggestion: Risk register (risks identified, assessed by likelihood × impact, mitigation actions with status and owner); Context analysis record (internal factors: staff, equipment, methods; external: regulatory, market, customer); Management review records showing risk items discussed and actions closed
notes: SR-01 §8.5 supplements ISO 17025 §8.5 by referencing §4.1 and explicitly requiring demonstration of context analysis, identification, assessment, and control actions. The standard text: 'Refer to 4.1. Lab shall demonstrate analysis of context, identification and assessment of risks and opportunities, and appropriate actions to control them.' Assessors will look for an active, maintained risk register — not a one-time document.

description: Plan and execute an internal audit programme with a schedule spanning 12 months, covering all ISO/IEC 17025 technical and management requirements. Ensure auditors are competent (trained in auditing techniques and in the relevant technical area) and independent from the activities being audited. Maintain all audit records: programme, audit plan, audit notes/evidence, audit report, and corrective actions raised and closed.
evidenceSuggestion: Annual internal audit programme / schedule (all clauses and methods covered within 12 months); Auditor competence records (training certificate, independence confirmation); Audit plan per audit; Completed audit checklists with objective evidence noted; Audit report (findings classified by severity); Corrective action records linked to findings; Closure evidence
notes: SR-01 §8.8 supplements ISO 17025 §8.8. AOSC requires specific records: programme, plan, audit notes, audit report, and corrective actions — all five must exist. Auditor competence is an explicit AOSC check. Recommended: complete the annual audit at least 2 months before the AOSC assessment so all corrective actions can be closed and verified before the assessor arrives.

description: The laboratory's top management shall review the effectiveness of the management system at least once every 12 months. The management review must cover the inputs required by ISO 17025 §8.9.2 (audit results, PT trends, corrective actions, customer feedback, resource adequacy, risk update, etc.) and produce documented outputs: decisions and actions with owners and deadlines. Retain management review records for at least 5 years.
evidenceSuggestion: Management review meeting agenda (covering all §8.9.2 inputs); Signed meeting minutes with decisions and action items; Attendance records (confirming top management participation); Action item tracking log from previous review; Evidence of actions closed
notes: SR-01 §8.9 supplements ISO 17025 §8.9. The standard text: 'Effectiveness reviewed at least once per 12 months.' This is the minimum frequency — the lab may review more often. 'Effectiveness' means the review must assess whether the MS is actually working, not just whether required activities were completed. Include SA1 NC closure status and SA2 preparation as standing agenda items during the 2025–2030 cycle.

description: Maintain a method SOP for each accredited test that includes: (1) reference to the applicable standard and edition year, (2) equipment and reagent requirements, (3) sample preparation steps, (4) step-by-step test procedure, (5) calculation formulae, (6) QC acceptance criteria, and (7) safety and waste disposal. Ensure SOPs are approved before use, version-controlled, and readily accessible at the point of testing.
evidenceSuggestion: SOPs for all accredited methods (current version, approved and signed); SOP checklist confirming all 7 elements present; Document control records (revision history, approval signatures, distribution); Evidence SOPs are available at test bench (printed controlled copy or electronic access)
notes: This row captures the SOP documentation requirements under SR-01 §7.2.1. While SR-01 doesn't explicitly enumerate the 7 SOP elements, these derive from the requirement to have 'documented methods referenced, verified, validated, and quoted in reports' combined with ISO 17025 §7.2.1. Assessors audit SOPs against the actual standard method and will flag if a procedure deviates without documented justification.

description: Maintain documented procedures for: (1) acquisition of reference materials (RM) — selection criteria, supplier evaluation, order specification; (2) preservation — storage conditions, handling precautions, stability monitoring; (3) maintenance — inspection schedule, cleaning requirements; (4) confirmation — verification of RM suitability and traceability before use. All four procedures must be documented and followed for CRMs, working standards, and check standards used in accredited testing.
evidenceSuggestion: RM management procedure (covering all four steps: acquisition, preservation, maintenance, confirmation); RM storage condition records (temperature/humidity logs where applicable); RM stability check/confirmation records; RM disposal records for expired materials
notes: SR-01 §6.5 explicitly requires documented procedures for all four RM lifecycle phases. This is often covered in a single 'Reference Material Management Procedure'. Key practical point: CRMs stored beyond their certified expiry date must not be used for accredited testing even if the material appears unchanged. The certificate validity date is binding.

description: Maintain a current copy of AOSC GR-02 (Use of Accreditation Symbol) and review all test report templates against GR-02 requirements after every accreditation assessment and whenever GR-02 is revised. Where a test report includes both accredited and non-accredited results, the scope of accreditation must be clearly delineated in the report so customers can distinguish which results carry accredited status.
evidenceSuggestion: Current AOSC GR-02 document on file (version-controlled); Test report template review checklist against GR-02 requirements; Sample issued reports with mixed accredited/non-accredited results showing clear delineation; Customer notification procedure for report template changes
notes: SR-01 §7.8 supplementary note: GR-02 is the AOSC guidance document for accreditation symbol use. It specifies exact format, placement, and prohibited uses of the VILAT/VLAC symbols. Template review is needed after SA1 and before SA2 to ensure compliance is maintained. Obtain the latest GR-02 from AOSC directly or from their website.

text: ANNEX I — EQUIPMENT CALIBRATION INTERVALS (SR-01 Annex I)

description: Gas Chromatograph — CL-2017-001, CL-2018-001 (Agilent 8890 GC, Da Vinci): Calibrate temperature-controlling systems (column oven, injector, detector) annually via a VILAS-accredited calibration lab. Verify GC detector response and linearity by running a certified reference standard before each analytical sequence. Record calibration certificates and detector performance data in each instrument's history file.
evidenceSuggestion: Annual calibration certificates for GC temperature systems (CL-2017-001 and CL-2018-001); Detector linearity / calibration curve records per analysis run; GC equipment history files
notes: SR-01 Annex I (Gas Chromatograph — temperature). Max calibration interval: 1 year. Verify exact item number against current SR-01 Annex I. Temperature calibration points: at least at the programmed column oven set-point and injector temperature used in accredited methods.

description: Pressure Gauge — CL-2034-001, CL-2035-001 (Nuova Fima, EN837-1): Submit each pressure gauge to a VILAS-accredited calibration lab for annual calibration covering the full working range used in testing. Verify that the calibration certificate includes measurement uncertainty and a traceability statement to SI. Apply correction factors from the certificate where gauge error exceeds method tolerance.
evidenceSuggestion: Annual calibration certificates for CL-2034-001 and CL-2035-001 (pressure range calibrated, measurement uncertainty stated); Correction factor records if applied; Equipment history files
notes: SR-01 Annex I (Pressure Gauge). Max calibration interval: 1 year. Verify exact item number against current SR-01 Annex I. EN837-1 Bourdon tube gauges: accuracy class must meet method requirement. Inspect for physical damage (cracked glass, bent pointer) before each use.

description: Analytical Balance — CL-2044-001 (Mettler Toledo MS304TS/00, 320 g, 0.1 mg): Submit to a VILAS-accredited calibration lab annually for full calibration (linearity across range, repeatability, eccentricity, minimum weighing capacity). Perform a daily single-point check using a class E2 or F1 reference weight before each day of use; record the reading and acceptance/rejection outcome.
evidenceSuggestion: Annual calibration certificate (CL-2044-001) from VILAS-accredited lab; Daily balance check log (date, reference weight used, balance reading, tolerance, pass/fail, person); Reference weight calibration certificate
notes: SR-01 Annex I (Analytical Balance). Max external calibration interval: 1 year. Verify exact item number against current SR-01 Annex I. Daily check tolerance: ±0.0002 g (0.2 mg) for class I analytical balance. Reference weights must themselves be calibrated (class E2 or F1) with valid certificate.

description: Extrusion Plastometer Temperature System — CL-5001 to CL-5005 series (Zwickroell Mflow, 5 units): Calibrate the temperature sensor / thermocouple in each MFI tester cylinder annually via a VILAS-accredited calibration lab. Verify actual cylinder temperature at each test setpoint used (e.g., 190 °C and 230 °C per ISO 1133). Tolerance: ±0.5 °C at setpoint (per ISO 1133). Apply a correction if deviation exceeds tolerance.
